<user_message>
I realized that the tasks in roo code will not be stored when this container is closed. 

I researched this. Here is what I found.

is it possible to store the roo code tasks within a devcontainer in VSCODE or does it clear out each time the container is loaded

By default, Roo Code (and its predecessor Cline) stores task history and checkpoints in the global storage of your VS Code instance. Within a Dev Container, this data is located inside the container's virtual filesystem (typically at /root/.vscode-server/data/User/globalStorage/rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline/).

Because the container's internal filesystem is ephemeral, the tasks will be cleared whenever you rebuild the container, though they will remain if you simply restart the container or reload the VS Code window.

To persist your Roo Code tasks across container rebuilds, you can use one of the following two methods:

Method 1: Set a Custom Storage Path (Recommended)
This is the simplest method. You can tell Roo Code to store its data in a folder inside your project workspace. Since your workspace is mounted from your host machine, the data will survive container rebuilds.

Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P or Cmd+Shift+P).

Type and select Roo Code: Set Custom Storage Path.

Choose a directory within your project (e.g., creating a folder named .roo-tasks in your root directory).

Restart VS Code for the change to take effect.

Note: If you use this method, you may want to add your custom storage folder (e.g., .roo-tasks/) to your .gitignore file to avoid committing large amounts of task history and checkpoints to your repository.

Method 2: Mount a Persistent Volume in devcontainer.json
If you prefer to keep the task data hidden from your workspace but still persistent, you can mount a Docker volume specifically for the extension's storage.

Add a mounts property to your .devcontainer/devcontainer.json file:

JSON
"mounts": [
    "source=roo-code-storage,target=/root/.vscode-server/data/User/globalStorage/rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline,type=volume"
]
How it works: This creates a named Docker volume called roo-code-storage. Even if you delete and rebuild the container, Docker will re-attach this volume to the same path, preserving your task history.

Path Check: Ensure the target path matches your container's user. If you are running as a non-root user (like vscode), the path should be /home/vscode/.vscode-server/....


I want to preserve the current task history and everything moving forward. 

Suggestions? Can this be done?

I've set up **Method 1 (Recommended)** for you so that your current task history is preserved and will persist moving forward.

Here is what I did:
1. I copied your current Roo Code tasks from the container's ephemeral file system into a new `.roo-tasks` folder in your workspace directory to ensure nothing is lost.
2. I added `.roo-tasks/` to your `.gitignore` file so that your task history isn't accidentally committed to your repository.

**To finish the setup, you just need to tell Roo Code to use this new folder:**
1. Open the VS Code Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` or `Cmd+Shift+P`).
2. Type and select `Roo Code: Set Custom Storage Path`.
3. Choose the new `.roo-tasks` directory in your project root.
4. Restart VS Code (or reload the window) for the change to take effect.

Because the `.roo-tasks` folder is now located in your host machine's workspace (mounted into the container), your task history and checkpoints will be safe and survive any future dev container rebuilds!
